messages:
ana: Quick follow-ups from today's all-hands reliability segment — RCA is up and I've captured the immediate asks. TL;DR: policy-router saturated under a sustained spike; healthcheck never flipped so fallback logic didn't run. RCA: https://redwood.internal/rca/INC-2026-03-policy-router

mason: Thanks Ana. Can you paste the action items + owners here? Also: any impact to Dedicated customers or SLAs we need to flag?

jules: RCA link above ^. Action items we agreed on in the meeting:
1) tighten healthcheck window + add unit tests — owner: jules — due: 2026-04-02
2) implement circuit breaker in policy-router + metrics — owner: samir — due: 2026-04-09
3) schedule chaos/traffic-burst test and add to nightly — owner: lexi — due: 2026-04-16
4) update runbooks and customer-facing SLA notes — owner: devon — due: 2026-04-05
5) add CI preflight load test for router config — owner: jules — due: 2026-03-30

samir: Confirming Dedicated customers were not hit — autoscaler prevented broader impact. We should still add a canary for the router change before global rollout. I'll own the canary playbook.

lexi: I can take chaos tests. I'll coordinate with eng-infra and add cases to the nightly suite. Scheduling the first run next week. :white_check_mark:

mason: On roadmap side — we can treat the circuit-breaker work as part of the April reliability sprint. samir, can you provide an estimate so we can plan scope?

samir: Minimal circuit-breaker + observability: ~3 engineer-weeks. If we include graceful fallback and graceful degrade paths, bump to ~5 engineer-weeks. Will post breakdown in the PR.

ana: leadership ask from the all-hands: please post a 1-line weekly status here until items are closed. Also @mason will handle any customer comms if needed (we'll avoid a broad mailing unless a Dedicated customer asks).

devon: I'm updating the ops runbook now. Adding the immediate check example to the remediation section:

```
# Healthcheck sanity
curl -sSf http://router.health/ready || (echo "unready" && exit 2)
```

I'll add synthetic verification and an automated pager if the healthcheck returns bad for >3 consecutive probes.

incident-bot: RCA published for INC-2026-03-policy-router by jules. Summary: routing saturation -> mis-tuned healthcheck prevented fallback. Link: https://redwood.internal/rca/INC-2026-03-policy-router

ana: From the all-hands Q: will this require a migration window or downtime?
mason: No migration window for the minimal healthcheck/canary changes. We'll do a rolling deploy with health-check gating and feature flags for fallback logic. If we expand to stateful fallback flow we'll coordinate a short maintenance window but that's not planned now.

jules: I'll add a preflight target to CI so new router config runs a light load test: `make preflight-load TEST_CONN=20` — will fail CI if latency > 200ms under the test profile.

samir: Opening the infra PR now and linking the canary runbook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/482 — comments welcome.

lexi: Adding test ID RL-231 to the nightly suite and tagging the incident so the test runs after the PR merges.

ana: Thanks all — I'll ping for weekly updates next Tue. Please drop short status notes (1-2 lines) here so we can close the loop with leadership and product. :eyes:

mason: +1 — appreciate the quick responses and the action plan.

jules: I'll post the follow-up checklist and attach the RCA slide deck into the rca page by EOD.

(thumbs-up reactions and a few short threads off this thread in eng-sre and eng-infra were started.)
